title: Exercise and pharmacotherapy in the treatment of major depressive disorder
authors: Blumenthal JA, Babyak MA, Doraiswamy PM, Watkins L, Hoffman BM, Barbour KA, et al.
population: Adults with major depressive disorder at a US tertiary teaching hospital, 2000 to 2005, randomised to supervised group aerobic exercise (51), home-based aerobic exercise (53), sertraline 50 to 200 mg (49) or placebo (49)
funder: This research was supported by Grant MH 49679 from the National Institutes of Health and NIH Grant MO1-RR-30 from the National Center for Research Resources. Medication and matched placebo pills were provided by a grant from Pfizer Pharmaceuticals; Pfizer had no other role in the study design, data acquisition, data analysis, or preparation of this manuscript.
inKindSupport: Sertraline and matching placebo provided by Pfizer.
authorConflicts: Blumenthal previously received a Pfizer/Eisai grant for an unrelated study; Doraiswamy reported grants and honoraria from several antidepressant manufacturers, including Pfizer.
result: Remission (no MDD diagnosis and HAM-D below 8) at 16 weeks: supervised exercise 45%, home exercise 40%, sertraline 47%, placebo 31% (p=0.057); HAM-D scores of active groups did not differ significantly from placebo (p=0.23). No treatment by severity interaction; with baseline HAM-D of 18 or more, remission 44%, 30%, 39% and 27%.
